title: Range Sum Query 2D - Immutable
statement: Build a structure over a fixed matrix that answers repeated rectangle-sum queries. SumRegion returns the total of every cell between (row1, col1) and (row2, col2) inclusive. The matrix never changes, and there may be many thousands of queries, so each one must be O(1).
constraints: 0 <= row1 <= row2 < rows and 0 <= col1 <= col2 < cols
hints: Summing the rectangle per query is O(rows*cols) each time. Since the matrix is immutable, pay once in the constructor instead.

Precompute a table where entry (i, j) holds the sum of the whole rectangle from the origin to (i, j). Building it is one pass with the same add-the-neighbours-subtract-the-overlap idea you will use to query it.

Then a query is inclusion-exclusion: whole - above - left + the top-left corner added back, because subtracting both strips removes their overlap twice. Pad the table with an extra leading row and column of zeros and the boundary cases stop needing special handling.
complexity: O(rows*cols) to build, O(1) per query

members: int SumRegion(int row1, int col1, int row2, int col2)
